env.head: a4708c8
env.driver: safaridriver 27.0.1, W3C WebDriver: POST /url, then POST /execute/async (script timeout 400000 ms)
env.window: Safari frontmost (open -a Safari), document visible for the whole run, CSS inner 1200x689, dpr 2, canvas 1960x1248 (CSS 980x624) as in Chrome's M2/M3/M6, rAF 60 Hz (Chrome: 120 Hz on this display)
env.power: AC Power, battery 100% charged, lowpowermode 0, caffeinate -dimsu running
env.chromeIdle: both Chrome MCP servers on about:blank

runOrder: every tab but Audio in the tab-bar order, then Audio alone, on the same page: without a user gesture (the runner's in-page tab.click() is not one) Audio setup never reaches its 4th check, which calls engine.audio.suspend() then resume() (most likely AudioContext.resume(), which Safari's autoplay policy holds until a gesture; the exact point was not measured), and the SectionSwitcher (one switch at a time) would hold every later tab on the Audio panel (see attempt1BlockedByAudio in m12-tabs-B.json)

attempt1BlockedByAudio.what: first Mode B run, every tab in the tab-bar order: after Audio every tab shows the Audio panel (3 checks, Suspend/resume never reported), because Audio setup never ends and the SectionSwitcher serialises switches

audioWithTrustedClick.what: fresh ?mode=B page; the Audio tab clicked through WebDriver Element Click (POST /element/{id}/click on "#tab-bar .tab:nth-child(4)", text "Audio"), a trusted click that is a user gesture; read 6 s later
audioWithTrustedClick.reading: with a real gesture Audio equals Chrome (4/4) and the AudioContext runs: the hang of the automated run is consistent with the autoplay policy (AudioContext.resume() waits for a gesture)
